text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Independent MP Rolf Patel on Tuesday irked parliament currently sitting in Zomba without opposition parties when he refused to support a bill to borrow Malawi Kwacha 45-million ($3-million) from Kuwait after accusing cabinet ministers of pocketing migrant labour funds.

- British and American experts said a government Plant and Vehicle Hire Organisation was unable to provide services of acquiring and repairing government vehicles and had instead forced other government departments to use private facilities.

- Opposition parties Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and Alliance for Democracy currently boycotting parliament said speaker of the National Assembly Rodwell Munyenyembe had ridiculed his office by announcing that he did not sanction the boycott.

- More than 200 ruling United Democratic Front party supporters on Tuesday marched in the streets of Blantyre and petitioned the High Court to reverse its ruling restraining the Electoral Commission from conducting by-elections on December 23 after an application by the main opposition MCP.
